head: Orthant: free window manager for Windows 11 and Mac with custom layouts
dek: Orthant is a free, open-source app that puts a grid over your screen: you drag across it to choose where a window goes, then save that spot to a keyboard shortcut. It comes with 11 ready shortcuts for halves, quarters, maximize and center, and you can change all of them.
details: Regions you draw can be named and keep their share of the screen if you change the grid later. The grid shows on every display, so you can also send a window to another screen. It runs from the menu bar on a Mac and the notification area on Windows. It's made by Owen Ou and published under the MIT licence; version 1.2.0 is the latest.
where: Free download for macOS 13 or later and 64-bit Windows 10 (version 1809 or later) or Windows 11; no Linux
means: If snapping windows to halves isn't enough for you, Orthant lets you set up your own layouts and jump to them with a key.
todo: On a Mac, allow it under Privacy & Security, then Accessibility, when it asks; it needs that to move windows. On Windows, if SmartScreen stops the installer, choose More info, then Run anyway.
